note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md (2026-11-28): 11 pictures chosen from 24 trial pictures. Wide pictures only (1920x1088). Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper 60% of the frame, clear of the word box. God and the angels are not pictured; Abraham, Sarah, Lot, Hagar, Abimelech and the others are only ordinary people of today, seen from behind, small, or as hands. Fixed recurring objects: Abraham's tent is a small plain weathered tan canvas tent on a simple wooden pole frame; the oak is one huge old oak with a broad gnarled trunk and a wide dark-green crown; Abimelech's town is a walled town of plain flat-roofed pale stone houses with a heavy timber gate, no church, no dome, no steeple and no tower of any kind; the king's hall is a plain large room of pale stone with a long wooden table.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning; (2) write picture ideas for each; (3) judge them; (4) make the top two for each slot as real pictures and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: Abraham moves to Gerar and says of Sarah, 'She is my sister', and Abimelech takes her.
God warns Abimelech in a dream that the woman is married and that Abraham, a prophet, will pray for him.
Abimelech tells his servants, then confronts Abraham, who explains his fear and half-truth.
Abimelech gives Sarah back with flocks and silver; Abraham prays, and God heals Abimelech's household.

scenes.principle: And Abraham traveled from there to the land of the Negev, and he lived between Kadesh and Shur, and he stayed in Gerar.
scenes.shows: A man leads a flock and a tent camp south across dry land.
scenes.prompt: Seen from a distance, a small traveling household with a flock of sheep moving south over dry rolling Negev scrubland under a huge sky, a rolled a small plain weathered tan canvas tent on a simple wooden pole frame on a donkey, in the upper part of the frame.

scenes.principle: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, "She is my sister." And Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.
scenes.shows: A man whispers anxiously to a woman at a town gate.
scenes.prompt: Seen from behind and slightly side, an anxious older ordinary man bending close to whisper to his wife at the gate of a walled town of plain flat-roofed pale stone houses with a heavy timber gate, no church, no dome, no steeple and no tower of any kind, his hand half raised near his mouth, soft daylight, upper part of frame.

scenes.principle: And God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said to him, "Look, you are about to die because of the woman you have taken, for she is a married woman."
scenes.shows: A man sleeps while a soft bright light fills the dark room, no figure.
scenes.prompt: A man asleep in a plain large bed in a dark stone room, a soft bright pure white-gold light entering through the window and filling the room, no figure in the light, upper part of frame.

scenes.principle: Did he not himself say to me, 'She is my sister'? And she herself also said, 'He is my brother.' In the blamelessness of my heart and the innocence of my palms I did this."
scenes.shows: Two open empty palms held out.
scenes.prompt: Close view of two open, empty, clean palms held out in a gesture of innocence against a soft dark background of a stone room, golden window light.

scenes.principle: And Abimelech rose early in the morning and called all his servants and spoke all these words in their ears, and the men were very afraid.
scenes.shows: A row of servants stand pale and afraid in a stone hall at dawn.
scenes.prompt: A row of ordinary servants standing close together in a pale stone hall at dawn with pale frightened faces, a man speaking to them from the far end, all in the upper part of the frame.

scenes.principle: And Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, "What have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? Deeds that are not done you have done to me."
scenes.shows: Two men face each other across a table, one with open hands in anger, the other looking down.
scenes.prompt: Two ordinary men at a long plain wooden table in a stone hall, one standing leaning on the table with open questioning hands, the other, an older man, sitting looking down at his hands, upper part of frame.

scenes.principle: And besides, she truly is my sister, the daughter of my father, only not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife.
scenes.shows: Two figures walk side by side, one half hidden by the other, a half-true story.
scenes.prompt: A half-lit stone wall with a man's long shadow and a woman's shadow beside it, two shadows only, half in light and half in dark, no people visible, upper part of frame.

scenes.principle: And Abimelech took flocks and cattle and male slaves and female slaves and gave them to Abraham, and he gave Sarah his wife back to him.
scenes.shows: Flocks and cattle are led out of a gate and a woman is given back to a man's outstretched hand.
scenes.prompt: A man's outstretched hand receiving a woman's hand from another man's hand at the gate of a walled town of plain flat-roofed pale stone houses with a heavy timber gate, no church, no dome, no steeple and no tower of any kind, a flock of sheep and cattle being led out through the gate behind, upper part of frame.

scenes.principle: And to Sarah he said, "Look, I have given a thousand pieces of silver to your brother. Look, it is for you a covering of the eyes for all who are with you, and with everyone you are cleared."
scenes.shows: A leather pouch of silver on a table next to a folded veil.
scenes.prompt: A heavy leather pouch of silver pieces spilling a few coins on a plain wooden table beside a folded plain cloth veil, soft window light, no people.

scenes.principle: And Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his female servants, and they bore children.
scenes.shows: A man kneels and prays under an open sky while a household watches.
scenes.prompt: An old ordinary man kneeling with his hands open and his head bowed at the edge of a field under a huge evening sky, a small household standing at a respectful distance behind him, upper part of frame.

scenes.principle: For Yahweh had completely held back every womb of Abimelech's household, over the matter of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
scenes.shows: A row of empty cradles in a quiet house.
scenes.prompt: A row of empty plain wooden cradles in a quiet stone room, soft grey light through one window, no people, upper part of frame.
